target_statement: Generalize the shifted-Psi pole-killing ramp into an abstract scaled-kernel boundary calculus; classify minimal higher-order exponential, endpoint-flat, fractional, and compact Chebyshev pole annihilators; and identify the exact Dirichlet-series hypotheses under which the calculus and Landau exclusion transfer.
claim_status_sought: PROJECT_PROVED_THEOREM_WITH_SCOPE for abstract asymptotics and finite-dimensional filter algebra; CONDITIONAL_TRANSFER_THEOREM for general Dirichlet series; METHOD_OBSTRUCTION for positivity and inverse stability
trust_model: ANALYTIC_MANUSCRIPT_UNREFEREED for Stieltjes and asymptotic theorems
IMPORTED_FROM_LITERATURE only for named L-function applications and effective PNT inputs
first_unproved_edge: A general kernel-jet expansion with explicit minimal hypotheses, followed by a closed-form order-m pole-killer classification and its oscillation/instability tax
mask_or_node_class: Abstract locally finite Stieltjes measure for the analytic theorem; distinct nonnegative exponential rates for rational filters; Jacobi-type compact weights and finite real Chebyshev notch systems for the two-edge extension; actual von Mangoldt data only as one specialization
source_data_retained: The centered discrepancy A(t)=-C+E(t), every required moment/tail hypothesis on E, the full kernel phi, and the complete pole principal part are retained
coefficient_cone_and_sign: No positivity is assumed for the abstract discrepancy; the one-sided Landau corollary applies only to a real filtered function. Positivity of the underlying coefficients is recorded separately when used for growth or L-function applications
normalization: Scaled kernel K_delta(t,u)=exp(delta*u) phi(delta*(t-u)); the original slice has phi(0)=1, while endpoint-flat order alpha is normalized by phi(v)~v^alpha/Gamma(alpha+1); order-m pole killing means Laplace(phi) has a zero of order m at the chosen anchor
height_window_and_one_sided_floor: Boundary asymptotics use t=c/delta with c in compact subsets of (0,infinity); singularity exclusion fixes delta>0 and requires an eventual one-sided bound for all large t
quantifier_order: For the boundary theorem choose the kernel and compact c-window, then delta tends to zero. For Landau choose one fixed delta and kernel, then the inequality holds for every sufficiently large t
resolution_required: Exact Stieltjes identity, all retained discrepancy moments, exact rational multiplier zeros, and explicit distinction between compact-c asymptotics and unbounded-c eventual behavior

rate_and_exponent_ledger.order_m_inverse_instability: a zero of order m at q=delta produces exp(delta*t) times a polynomial of degree m-1
tail_regimes: integrable E gives an integer first correction delta*K0
rapid E gives the full moment expansion
regularly varying nonintegrable E may give fractional or delta*log(1/delta) corrections

feasibility_or_nonvacuity_witness: The zeta weighted-Mertens discrepancy and the already verified two-exponential filter satisfy the hypotheses; equally spaced rates give explicit order-m filters for every m
downstream_socket: The abstract theorem explains mesoscopic sign fronts and supplies exact pole-sensitive filters. A separate eventual one-sided theorem is still required to exclude singularities or zeta zeros
parallel_open_siblings: zeta-specific adjacent-support propagation in the Weil architecture
why_not_target_renamed: No compact-c boundary expansion is called a strip. General one-sided Landau criteria are labeled sufficient rather than equivalent unless a converse is separately proved
abstract_convex_falsifier: Test arbitrary E with compact support, polynomial tails, and oscillatory tails; test kernels in the pole-killing ideal against the positive cone
fejer_falsifier: For order m, verify the m moment constraints and at least m sign changes; failure indicates a normalization or multiplicity error
prime_density_pseudonode_falsifier: Insert a positive oscillatory density with a forbidden Mellin pole and verify that every claimed generic eventual margin fails
finite_actual_prime_diagnostic: Use only to replay the m=1 specialization and illustrate higher-order kernel zeros; no asymptotic claim is licensed by finite data
actual_prime_arithmetic_line: Any strip application beyond the abstract criterion must use arithmetic not shared by generic positive Mellin-pole models
decision_tree_change_if_proved: Promote the boundary layer from a zeta-specific identity to a reusable pole-filter calculus and identify exactly which parts can transfer to other zeta/L-functions
decision_tree_change_if_refuted: Retain only the verified m=1 zeta theorem and reject higher-order or general-L-function language
stop_rule: Stop extending a branch when it requires absent tail moments, complex quantities with no order, a pole/zero cancellation not represented in the multiplier, or an eventual estimate equivalent in strength to the desired singularity-free region
